p: Central has the greatest total wait, while Riverside Evening has the longest average wait. What follows?
c: One result must be an error
why: Total burden and individual experience are distinct questions.

p: Why show patient count beside an average wait?
c: The amount of supporting data affects interpretation
why: An average based on two observations has different context from one based on hundreds.

p: What is the denominator of over_60_rate?
why: The percentage describes the share of observed patients who waited over 60 minutes.

It removes the need for an ID

p: What is the role of clinic_id as a final sort key?
c: It proves one clinic is better
why: A stable identifier gives deterministic order after substantive criteria tie.

p: Why is a bar axis from 45 to 50 misleading for 46 and 48 minutes?
c: It exaggerates a two-minute difference in bar length
why: A truncated length scale removes the magnitude baseline.

p: Can clinic-level and clinic-time-slot rows be placed in one ranking?
why: Every ranked row must represent the same kind of unit.

p: What should a missing weekly record be treated as?
why: Absence of a record does not establish a zero value.

p: Which code calculates a combined service over-60 percentage after aggregation?
why: The aggregated affected count is divided by the aggregated population count.
